excerpt: Local SEO for remodelers isn't complicated, but it does reward consistency more than almost any other marketing channel. Here's where to focus first.
body:
Local SEO tends to get treated as either mysterious or oversimplified — either "the algorithm is unknowable" or "just get more reviews." Neither is quite right. For a remodeling company, local search rankings are influenced by a fairly specific, learnable set of factors, and a handful of them matter far more than the rest.

**Your Google Business Profile is doing more work than your website**

For local, service-based searches like "\[city] home remodeler" or "design build company near me," Google's map results often outrank the regular website listings entirely. A complete, active, accurate Google Business Profile — correct categories, service areas, updated photos, and regular posts — is frequently the single highest-leverage local SEO asset a remodeling company has, and it's also the one most commonly left half-finished.

**Reviews: quantity matters less than consistency**

A remodeler with 40 reviews at a steady pace of a few per month tends to outperform a remodeler with 80 reviews that all came from a single push two years ago and nothing since. Recency and consistency signal an active, currently operating business, which matters both to the algorithm and to a homeowner scrolling through results.

**Service-area pages, done honestly**

If you serve multiple cities or regions, dedicated pages for each area can help — but only when they contain genuinely different, useful content for that area (recent projects there, specific neighborhoods served, local considerations). Pages that are just the same template with the city name swapped tend to underperform, and in some cases can actively work against you.

**Citations and NAP consistency**

NAP — Name, Address, Phone — consistency across directories (Houzz, Angi, the Better Business Bureau, local chambers of commerce, industry associations) is a quieter factor, but inconsistent information across these listings can create confusion that dampens local ranking signals. This is unglamorous work, but it's also largely a one-time cleanup rather than an ongoing effort.

**Content that answers local, specific questions**

Generic content ("5 Tips for Your Kitchen Remodel") competes with thousands of similar pages nationwide. Content answering a specific local question — permitting timelines in your city, typical costs for your region, HOA considerations in a specific neighborhood — has far less competition and signals real local expertise, both to search engines and to the homeowner reading it.

**What to prioritize if you're starting from nothing**

In roughly this order: claim and fully complete your Google Business Profile, establish a simple, consistent system for requesting reviews after each project, clean up your NAP consistency across major directories, then move to service-area and locally-specific content once the fundamentals are solid.

**Why this is a slow-compounding channel, not a quick one**

Local SEO rarely produces a dramatic before-and-after. It's closer to a savings account than a lever — small, consistent deposits (reviews, accurate listings, relevant content) that compound over months, not days. That's exactly why it's easy to neglect and why the remodelers who stay consistent with it end up with a meaningful, durable advantage over ones who treat it as a one-time project.
